correctness.rationale: For U=P Sigma Q^T, orthogonal similarity by diag(P,Q) gives [[i gamma I,Sigma],[Sigma,-i gamma I]], then a coordinate permutation yields blocks B_j=[[i gamma,sigma_j],[sigma_j,-i gamma]]. Each satisfies B_j^2=(sigma_j^2-gamma^2)I. At gamma=sigma_j>0 the block is nonzero rank-one nilpotent with square zero, hence J_2(0); repeated singular values give independent copies. At gamma=0 zero singular values are semisimple. The algebraic proof is complete.
